raw_text:
Thanks — here's a focused 12-week strength program you can give your 27 y/o male beginner training in a small flat with only a yoga mat and a doorway pull-up bar. The plan prioritises progressive overload using bodyweight variations, frequency, and simple progression strategies (more reps, slower tempo, added sets, harder variations). It also includes warm-ups, mobility, recovery and basic nutrition guidance.

Structure and progression overview
- Frequency: 4 sessions per week (upper/lower split) — manageable for a beginner and effective for strength gains.
- Blocks: 3 × 4-week blocks (Build → Intensify → Consolidate/Peak). Each block increases intensity by adding reps, sets, harder exercise variations, tempo manipulation, and shorter rest.
- Sessions: A = Upper (horizontal push/pull + vertical push/pull + core); B = Lower (hinge, squat, single-leg, core). Two upper and two lower sessions per week (e.g., Mon/Thu = Upper, Tue/Fri = Lower) with 48–72 hours between similar sessions.
- Progression rules: If client completes target sets × reps with good form for two consecutive workouts, advance to the next progression (harder variation or add set/reps). If they cannot complete target, use an easier variation or increase rest.
- Reps & intensity: Work primarily in a 4–12 rep range for strength/hybrid strength-hypertrophy as a beginner. Use slower tempos on eccentric (3–4s) to increase time under tension when exercises are easy.
- Warm-up & cool-down: 5–10 minute dynamic warm-up each session plus light mobility and 3–5 minute cool-down stretch.
- Track: Have the client log sets, reps, perceived exertion and any form notes.

Equipment-limited exercise list (variations to use)
- Pull-up bar: dead hang, assisted pull-ups (one foot on chair/looped towel), negative-only slow eccentrics, chin-ups, neutral grip, wide/close grip
- Floor: push-ups (knees, incline using wall/doorframe, standard, diamond, archer/one-arm progressions), plank variations
- Isometrics & tempos: paused reps, slow eccentrics, isometric holds (top/mid/bottom)
- Single-leg: Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on chair/sofa), reverse lunges, pistol progressions (assisted)
- Hinge: single-leg Romanian deadlift (bodyweight, reaching), hip hinge with emphasis on glutes/hamstrings
- Core: dead bugs, hollow body, side plank, Russian twist (bodyweight), hanging knee raises, leg raises (progress to toes to bar)
- Calisthenics skill: active hang, scapular pull-ups, skin-the-cat progressions if possible

Weekly layout (example)
- Mon: Upper A
- Tue: Lower A
- Wed: Rest / active recovery (walk, mobility)
- Thu: Upper B
- Fri: Lower B
- Sat: Active recovery / optional light skill work (mobility, extra core)
- Sun: Rest

Detailed 12-week plan

Block 1 — Weeks 1–4: Foundation (build movement quality, condition, base strength)
Goal: Learn patterns, build work capacity, practice core pulls/pushes, create baseline.

Guidelines for all sessions in Block 1
- Warm-up (before each session): 5 minutes dynamic (arm circles, bandless pull-apart with towel, leg swings, glute bridges, hip hinge drills), plus 1 set of the main lift at a lighter intensity (e.g., incline push-ups 8–10 reps as warm-up).
- Tempo: 2s concentric / 2s eccentric for most movements. For pull-ups start with controlled negatives: 5s eccentric if needed.
- Rest between sets: 60–90s.
- Aim RPE: 6–7/10.

Week 1
Upper A (Mon)
1. Incline push-ups (hands on wall/doorframe at first, progress to higher surface) — 4 sets × 8–12
2. Assisted chin-ups (foot on chair) or negatives (5s) — 4 sets × 4–6 (or 6–8 negative reps)
3. Horizontal row using towel over door frame / bodyweight inverted row (if possible) or Australian pulls using bar — 3 sets × 8–10
4. Pike push-up (elevate feet slightly if needed) or incline partial shoulder press — 3 × 6–8
5. Dead-hang scapular pulls (active hang to scapular retraction) — 3 × 10–15s holds
6. Plank — 3 × 30–45s

Lower A (Tue)
1. Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on low surface) — 4 × 8 each leg
2. Glute bridge (single-leg progression if able) — 4 × 8–12
3. Reverse lunges — 3 × 8 each leg
4. Single-leg Romanian deadlift (bodyweight, toes reach) — 3 × 8 each leg
5. Side plank — 3 × 25–40s each side
6. Light conditioning: 8–10 minutes steady-paced skipping or marching in place if wanted

Upper B (Thu)
1. Push-ups (knees or full depending) — 4 × 8–12
2. Assisted pull-ups / negatives — 4 × 4–6
3. Bent-over towel rows / Australian rows — 3 × 8–12
4. Diamond incline push-ups or close-grip push-ups — 3 × 6–8
5. Hanging knee raises or lying leg raises — 3 × 8–12
6. Farmer carry alternative: suitcase carry with backpack loaded (optional) — 3 × 30–45s each side

Lower B (Fri)
1. Bodyweight squat (progress to slow tempo and pauses) — 4 × 12–15 (2s up/2s down)
2. Bulgarian split squat — 3 × 8 each leg
3. Single-leg hip hinge (RDL) — 3 × 8 each leg
4. Calf raises (double and single-leg) — 4 × 12–15
5. Hollow hold / dead bug — 3 × 20–40s

Weeks 2–4: progress by increasing difficulty per exercise (move to floor push-ups from incline, reduce assistance on chin-ups, increase single-leg demands), add 1 set to major lifts in week 3, reduce rest to 60s by week 4. Emphasise controlled eccentrics (3–4s) on last two weeks.

Block 2 — Weeks 5–8: Intensify (increase load via harder variations, tempo changes and volume)
Goal: Build strength by introducing harder progressions, lower-rep strength sets on key lifts, and more specific pulling/pushing volume.

Guidelines
- Warm-up as before.
- Tempo: Introduce slow eccentrics 3–4s for main lifts, explosive concentric where appropriate.
- Rest: 90–120s for heavy sets (lower rep), 45–60s for accessory work.
- Aim RPE: 7–8/10.

Week 5 (example)
Upper A (Mon)
1. Full push-ups — 5 × 6–10 (if easy, add paused reps at bottom 2s)
2. Pull-ups/chin-ups: attempt unassisted or mixed set with negatives — 5 × 3–6 (use assisted if needed to hit reps)
3. Australian rows (lower bar or setup) — 4 × 8–12 with a 3s eccentric
4. Pike push-ups or elevated-feet push-ups — 4 × 6–8
5. Hanging knee raises → progress to bent-leg raises — 4 × 8–12
6. Side plank with leg lift — 3 × 30s each side

Lower A (Tue)
1. Narrow (or slow) bodyweight squat — 5 × 8–12 (include 2s pause at bottom on some sets)
2. Bulgarian split squat — 4 × 8–10
3. Single-leg RDL — 4 × 8 each leg, slow tempo
4. Glute bridge march / single-leg glute bridge — 4 × 8–10
5. Farmers carry with loaded backpack — 3 × 40–60s

Upper B (Thu)
1. Decline push-ups (feet on sofa/chair) or diamond push-ups — 5 × 6–8
2. Pull-up negatives + attempts or weighted-ish backpack chin-up (small) — 5 × 3–6
3. Towel rows over door or elevated Australian row — 4 × 10
4. Archer push-up progressions (assisted) — 3 × 4–6 each side
5. Hanging leg raises or supported toes-to-bar progression — 4 × 6–10
6. Hollow rock or advanced plank — 3 × 30–45s

Lower B (Fri)
1. Pistol progressions to box pistol or assisted pistol — 4 × 5–8 each leg
2. Reverse Nordic or slow eccentric knee flexor drill if available for quad strength — 3 × 6–8
3. Single-leg hip hinge — 4 × 8–10 each leg
4. Bulgarian split squat (heavier variation) — 3 × 6–8
5. Calf raises single-leg — 4 × 10–12
6. Plank variations — 3 × 45–60s

Weeks 6–8: continue to reduce assistance on pull-ups, introduce negatives with 5s eccentric until full reps achievable. Introduce "heavy" sets on primary lifts: 4–6 reps at near-max for bodyweight strength (i.e., hardest progression they can do). Increase sets to 5 on main compound movements by week 8.

Block 3 — Weeks 9–12: Consolidation and peak strength testing
Goal: Peak strength for bodyweight movements and consolidate gains. Aim to max out on pull-ups, push-ups and one-leg squat progressions.

Guidelines
- Focus on low reps for max strength: sets of 3–6 for main lifts, higher for accessory.
- Rest 120–180s for near-max attempts.
- Week 12: testing week — record max strict pull-ups, max full push-ups in one set (or max reps to failure in a strict cadence), and pistol reps per leg.

Week 9 (example)
Upper A (Mon)
1. Weighted-ish progressive push variation (elevate feet + slow eccentrics or vest alternative: loaded backpack) — 5 × 4–6
2. Pull-ups/chin-ups (unassisted): 6 × 3–5 (if able do reps across; otherwise assisted with fewer reps)
3. Australian rows weighted (pack) or feet elevated — 4 × 6–8
4. Handstand push-up progressions against wall or strict pike push-ups — 3 × 4–6
5. Hanging leg raises to toes progression — 4 × 8–12
6. L-sit hold (tuck) — 3 × 10–20s

Lower A (Tue)
1. Assisted pistol / full pistol (if ready) — 6 × 3–6 each leg
2. Single-leg Romanian deadlift — 5 × 6–8
3. Bulgarian split squat (slow eccentric) — 4 × 6–8
4. Glute bridge single-leg weighted (backpack) — 4 × 6–8
5. Core: Pallof press alternative with towel bracing, side plank — 3 × 30–45s

Upper B (Thu)
1. Max-effort push-ups (work up to heavy sets of 3–6) — 5 × 3–6
2. Pull-up volume (pyramid sets or 8× moderate sets) — 8 × 3–5 or 4×6 depending on fatigue
3. Towel rows / inverted rows — 4 × 6–8
4. Push-up variations: archer, pseudo planche leans — 3 × 4–6
5. Hanging toes-to-bar attempts — 4 × AMRAP controlled

Lower B (Fri)
1. Pistol sets — 6 × 3–6
2. Single-leg hip hinge heavy/slow — 5 × 6–8
3. Bulgarian split squat — 4 × 6
4. Calf single leg weighted — 4 × 8–10
5. Core: weighted hollow (pack) or prolonged plank — 3 × 45–60s

Weeks 10–11: Maintain high intensity; reduce volume slightly if fatigue accumulates. Increase rest for heavy sets. Add tempo negatives on pull-ups if sticking point is concentric — eccentric emphasis helps.

Week 12 — Test Week
- Reduce accessory volume and test maximal performance.
Testing protocol (pick 1–3 days with full rest between tests):
1. Strict pull-up max: after thorough warm-up, perform single-rep attempts to reach max strict reps (record).
2. Max strict push-ups in one set (or max across sets at same tempo).
3. Pistol/one-leg squat max reps per leg (or best single rep).
- After testing, prescribe 1 week light deload (active recovery) before next mesocycle.

Daily warm-up template (5–10 minutes)
- Joint circles, bandless pull-aparts with towel 2 × 10
- Cat-cow/hip hinge 10 reps
- Scapular shrugs on bar 2 × 10
- 1 set of the first movement at 50% intensity (e.g., incline push-ups × 8)

Mobility & recovery
- Encourage 2–3 weekly mobility sessions (10–15 min): thoracic rotations, pec stretch in doorframe, hip flexor stretch, hamstring mobility, ankle mobility.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours nightly.
- Active recovery: walking or light cycling on rest days.
- If delayed onset muscle soreness is high, reduce volume and increase rest.

Nutrition & bodyweight guidance (brief, beginner-friendly)
- Aim for a small calorie surplus if primary goal is strength and muscle: roughly +200–300 kcal/day above maintenance. If lean mass gain is desired with minimal fat, keep lean proteins high.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day (for a 27 y/o male beginner; e.g., if 75 kg aim for ~120–165g/day).
- Carbohydrate: sufficient for training (2.5–5 g/kg depending on activity). Emphasise carbs around workouts (pre/post).
- Fats: ~20–30% of calories.
- Hydration: 2–3 L/day baseline; more with sweat.
- Simple meal structure: protein + veg + carb per main meal; snack with protein post-workout if needed.

Coaching cues and form emphasis
- Pull-ups: active shoulder (“pack” shoulders), lead with chest, avoid kipping — use strict form.
- Push-ups: straight line from head to heels, retract scapula before lowering, avoid sagging hips.
- Single-leg: control descent, knee over toes tracking, hip hinge for balance.
- Hinge: push hips back, maintain neutral spine, feel glutes and hamstrings.
- When fatigue compromises form, stop the set and regress.

Troubleshooting & regressions
- If client cannot perform strict pull-ups after 8 weeks: use eccentric-only with slow 5–8s lowering for 4–6 reps × 4–6 sets, plus scapular pull-ups and assisted band/foot-assisted reps.
- If knees or joints complain: reduce range of motion, pause squats to a box, reduce volume, focus on hip hinge and glute activation.
- If recovery poor: cut sessions to 3×/week (full-body) for 2 weeks and then resume.

Sample micro-progression examples
- Push-up: incline → floor → paused → decline → archer → one-arm assisted.
- Pull-up: assisted foot → negatives 5s → mixed grip → unassisted 1–3 reps → sets of 3–6 → add volume.
- Pistol: box pistol → assisted pistol (hold doorframe) → eccentrics → unassisted.

Notes for you as trainer
- Encourage the client to log every session and report soreness, sleep, and nutrition weekly.
- Review technique via video at regular intervals (every 1–2 weeks early on).
- Adjust progression speed per individual response; some beginners adapt quickly, others need more time on regressions.

If you want, I can:
- Convert this into a printable week-by-week table or PDF.
- Provide exact daily sessions written out for each of the 12 weeks (with every set/reps for each day).
- Create a 3-day per week alternative for clients who can’t sustain 4 days.

Which of those would you like next?
